mentl/d4980fc:
The previous entry said the remaining 13 could not be fixed by widening,
because a with-clause cannot say Probe({record}). Measured: widening
`fn run() with Probe` to `with Probe + Memory + Alloc` clears the error
outright, leaving only a T_OverDeclared narration. The instance args never
blocked anything — eff_admits (effects.mn:1105) answers true for a bare
gate name against any instantiated body name, so a bare Probe admits
Probe(τ) by design and always has. Ten fixtures widened on that reading:
the payload family plus mn-ev2/mn-ev4. Battery errors 19 -> 9, carriers
eleven files -> four.

A second wrong turn the probe caught before it landed. `effect Probe {
emit(x) -> Int }` declares no parameter list, so I read Probe(Int) as
inference manufacturing an argument and was one edit from treating that as
the bug. infer.mn:8558 says the opposite in its own words: an effect's type
params ARE the free type vars across all its ops' signatures, so a
lowercase x declares one under the case rule. Removing it re-breaks what
that comment names — "the payload type never flows performer->handler...
the root of both the list-as-Int erasure and the emitter's heap-dump." A
two-file probe, annotated versus unannotated op arg, isolated the variable
and the site's own prose refuted the conclusion.

What remains is five reports in two fixtures, both named rather than
guessed. mn-feedback-iir's two are plausibly the known feedback-row
over-charge, and widening them would canonize an over-charge as a
fixture's declared truth. mn-backtrack-full's three are unread. Arming is
licensed when those five resolve.

The real surface bug is smaller than the one I claimed and still real:
T_OverDeclared advises an unwriteable row. Over a polymorphic op it
narrates "declares Probe but body only uses Probe(Int) — tighten the
signature", and `with Probe(Int)` does not parse. mentl tighten consumes
exactly these narrations, which is why the round-trip guard at pin
1aca4868 exists; the guard declines sil

mentl/d49597e:
Two coupled substrate fixes addressing the cfv→list_index→unreachable trap
that surfaced after #144 unblocked deeper execution paths:

1. WHEEL emit (src/backends/wasm.mn):
   - emit_lbinop arm now calls emit_binop_for(op, lexpr_handle(l)) instead
     of emit_binop(op). The new emit_binop_for handles BConcat by
     dispatching on the left operand's chase-deep Ty via perform lookup_ty:
     TList(_) → (call $list_concat), else → (call $str_concat). Mirrors
     the seed's emit_call.wat:283-323 dispatch per
     protocol_emit_is_graph_projection.md (emit reads the graph).
   - emit_binop retained as default for callers without operand handle
     (e.g., other arithmetic ops); the per-operand path branches to
     emit_binop_for from LBinOp's emit arm.

2. WHEEL lower (src/lower.mn cfv_merge):
   - Replaced `a ++ [x]` with explicit `list_concat(a, [x])` in the set-
     union recursion. Operand type inference for `a` (a fn parameter)
     resolves to NFree at infer time; BConcat's emit dispatch returned
     str_concat as the fall-through, treating the list bytes as a
     string. Downstream list_index walked the resulting "string" as a
     list, hit the tag-not-in-{0,1,3,4} unreachable.

Empirical proof:
- `fn main(x) = match x { [a, b] => a, _ => 0 }` through mentl2: was
  trap, now exit 0 with valid 1714-byte mentl3
- `cat src/main.mn | mentl2.wasm`: was trap, now exit 0 with 58KB
  output (interleaved diagnostics, but no trap)
- Wheel compile through seed: wat2wasm 0 errors (unchanged)
- mentl2 on full wheel: still emits empty-fallback (separate gate —
  wheel-emit-implementation cascade #111 — but no longer traps)

Composes with: protocol_call_indirect_paradox_2026_05_10.md (the
parent trap diagnosis), protocol_emit_is_graph_projection.md (emit
reads graph via lookup_ty), protocol_resume_state_mutation_substrate.md
(seed's existing emit_call.wat type-dispatch as the mirror reference).

sonido/d43bc30:
play and realtime commands created their own AtomicBool for the ctrlc
handler, separate from AudioStream's internal running flag. The handler
set the command's flag (silencing the callback) but never touched the
stream's spin loop — so run_output()/run() never returned. Second
Ctrl+C just printed "Stopping..." again.

Add AudioStream::running_handle() to expose the stream's Arc<AtomicBool>,
use it directly in both commands so a single flag controls callback,
spin loop, and signal handler.
tokensafe/d4bc04e:
The stored inflight promise had no .catch() handler, so when analysis
rejected (e.g. non-mint account on devnet), the rejection propagated
as unhandled and crashed the process. Replace Promise.race timeout
with clearTimeout cleanup in .finally() and add a no-op .catch()
on the stored promise — callers re-await and handle errors themselves.
